sources.entry: MacMorpheus - 3D 180/360 video player for macOS for PSVR with head tracking.

summary.one_liner: MacMorpheus is a macOS video player for 180° and 360° 3D videos that uses a PlayStation VR headset with head tracking.
summary.what_it_does: The app plays mp4, mov, and m4v video files in 2D 180°, 3D 360° horizontal (stacked), and 3D 180° vertical (side by side) formats, chosen from a dropdown when a video is opened. It sends the image to a PSVR headset connected over HDMI and uses USB from the PSVR processing box for head tracking. A second HDMI screen, such as a TV, can be connected in place of the headset. Keyboard controls handle fullscreen, play/pause, skipping, and recentering the view. Mouse drag lets you look around when not using the headset's tracking.
use_cases: watch 360 video in PSVR on a Mac
view side-by-side stereo video in a VR headset
use PlayStation VR as a display for macOS
play VR video with head tracking on a computer
how_to_run: Connect the HDMI cable from the PSVR headset to the computer; leave the other connector on the processing box.
Connect any other HDMI screen (such as a TV) in place of the headset; it must be on.
Connect USB from the PSVR processing box to the computer.
Launch the app, choose a video (mp4, mov, m4v), and select the correct format from the dropdown.
Press R to reset the view.
notable: Head tracking with PSVR hardware connected over USB
Keyboard controls for fullscreen, play/pause, skip, and view reset
caveats: Requires macOS and a PlayStation VR headset with its processing box, PS4, and HDMI/USB wiring
The README has a download section and a wiring diagram with no visible links or images, so download details are unclear
No license or build instructions are given in the README
